objective: Synthesize a path-sensitive use_after_free detector that encodes the same local state, guards, and lifecycle mechanism evidenced by the patch, while still generalizing to semantically equivalent sites.

semantic_dimensions: later use sink on the same resource
trigger_invariants: the same symbolic resource reaches a later use without reinitialization or ownership transfer
silence_invariants: the resource is nulled, rebound, or reinitialized before reuse
ownership transfer or guard logic blocks access after release
transfer_axes: equivalent release-then-use sequences on the same resource role
equivalent lifecycle transitions across wrappers or helper functions
equivalent guard or barrier predicates on sibling paths
equivalent local state transitions around the same sink or dereference
equivalent ownership or release/reinit lifecycle on the same symbolic resource
forbidden_shortcuts: bind the detector to fixed file paths, line numbers, or exact patch strings
broaden into unrelated bug families just to improve hit count
report every free/delete call as if it were a bug
ignore resource identity and alias continuity between release and use
identify resources only by variable or field names such as session/cache/context instead of lifecycle evidence
placeholder helper logic or empty ProgramState modeling

hypotheses: The patch likely changes a resource lifecycle or stale-state transition.
